- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots downward — reduce forecast dip by 5-10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 2-5% for next 5-7 days.  
- Model consistently underpredicts true price in early 30-day horizon — shift forecast upward by 1-3% for first 5 days to capture short-term volatility.  
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., > 0.7), model often fails to fully capture rally — add 2-5% buffer to forecast for next 7-10 days.  
- If recent 3-5 day price drop is followed by sentiment rebound, model often lags — forecast should rise 1-3 days ahead of true price.  
- Avoid over-relying on 30-day trend — sentiment shifts in 1-2 week windows often override longer-term forecasts — adjust horizon-specific forecasts to match sentiment cycle.
